faults.detail: Sub "4 equal gaps mein pehla mark" says the wave is about the first mark, but the wave's items are "1/4", "2/4", "3/4", "1/4": 2/4 and 3/4 are the second and third marks, so the label is wrong for half the wave.
Title "Aadha raasta" and sub "Do equal gaps ka middle mark" tell the child where every item of the wave ("1/2") goes before she catches it.
"4 equal gaps mein pehla mark" states the place of "1/4" (the first mark), which the wave asks the child to find.

notes: Every fraction is placed on a line whose gap count equals its denominator (2, 4, 5, 3), so a child who counts marks instead of gaps would misplace items and see why; the faults are the wave labels. Both screens are legible with nothing cut off; coach text "Dock ko drag karke mark pakdo" is dim grey but readable.

faults.detail: Title "Half mark" on a 2-gap line whose only items are "1/2" names the spot where the child must catch 1/2.

notes: Catching unit fractions one at a time on one 0-1 line puts 1/8 near 0 and 1/2 far from it, so a child who thinks 1/8 > 1/4 sees the belief fail; on topic. Waves 1 and 2 place fractions that do not sit on the drawn marks ("1/6", "1/3" on an 8-gap line; "1/8", "1/4" on a 6-gap line), which may confuse a class-5 child, and "precision": "safai" (cleanliness) is an odd word, but I do not count either as a fault.

faults.detail: The coach text "Grid par khet banao" is drawn over the top row of grid cells, and the goal pill "Daud 1/4 kshetrafal 40 varg ikai" butts against the bottom of the "KSHETRAFAL — / GHERA — / DAUD 1/4" pills: overlapping elements.

notes: All targets can be built on the 15x10 grid (area 40 as 8x5; perimeters 26, 20 and 38 as 8x5, 5x5 and 12x7) and match the topic keys. Building area 40 and then a different shape with perimeter 26 shows a child who multiplies for perimeter where she goes wrong. The labels are plain class-6 Hindi in Roman script ("kshetrafal", "ghera", "varg ikai"); "Daud" for round is unusual but understandable.
